chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Nadr ibn Wakee', from al-Rabee' ibn Sabeeh, who raised the narration to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) who said:

Whoever meets his brother with what pleases him, Allah will please him on the Day of Judgment; and whoever meets his brother with what displeases him to make him displeased, Allah will make him displeased on the Day he meets Him.

key_terms.أَخَاهُ: His brother (referring to a fellow believer)
key_terms.سَاءَهُ اللَّهُ: Allah will make him displeased / unhappy
key_terms.سَرَّهُ اللَّهُ: Allah will please him / make him happy

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of making a believer happy or sad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the spiritual reciprocity of social interactions, framing the act of pleasing a fellow believer as a direct cause for divine pleasure on the Day of Judgment. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *mu'amalat* (social conduct) as a pathway to *tawassul* (seeking nearness) to Allah, where human satisfaction mirrors divine satisfaction.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Ahmad b. Muhammad from Nadhar b. Wakee’ from al-Rabee’ b. Sabeeh who raised this narration to The Prophet (s.a.w.s.) who said: “
One who meets a believer to please him, Allah will make the former happy on the Day of Judgment. One who meets a believer to make him sad, Allah will make the former sad on the Day of Judgment.”
